[[Image:Exponential Parameter Space Detail PSP Rays.png|right|thumb|Parameter plane of the complex exponential family f(z)=exp(z)+c with 8 [[External ray|external ( parameter) rays]]]]
In the theory of [[dynamical system]]s, the '''exponential map''' can be used as the [[Dynamical system (definition)|evolution function]] of [[Recurrence relation|the discrete nonlinear dynamical system]].<ref>[https://macau.uni-kiel.de/receive/diss_mods_00000781?lang=en Dynamics of exponential maps by Lasse Rempe]</ref>

==Family==
The family of [[exponential function]]s is called the '''exponential family'''.

==Forms==
There are many '''forms''' of these maps,<ref>[http://arxiv.org/abs/0805.1658 "Bifurcation Loci of Exponential Maps and Quadratic Polynomials: Local Connectivity, Triviality of Fibers, and Density of Hyperbolicity"], [[Lasse Rempe]], Dierk Schleicher</ref> many of which are equivalent under a coordinate transformation. For example two of the most common ones are:

*<math>E_c : z \to e^z + c </math>
*<math>E_\lambda : z \to \lambda e^z</math>

The second one can be mapped to the first using the fact that <math>\lambda e^z = e^{z+\ln(\lambda)}</math>, so <math>E_\lambda : z \to e^z + \ln(\lambda)</math> is the same under the transformation <math>z=z+\ln(\lambda)</math>. The only difference is that, due to multi-valued properties of exponentiation, there may be a few select cases that can only be found in one version. Similar arguments can be made for many other formulas.
